Water leaking onto a patio forms a circular pool. The radius of the pool increases at a rate of $3\,\text{m/min}.$ How fast is the area of the pool increasing at the moment when the radius is $\frac{5}{2\pi }\,\text{m}?$

The area of the pool is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}} ${\text{m}}^{2}\text{/min}.$
question.worked_solution:
In this situation, we want to find $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}$ at the moment when $r=\frac{5}{2\pi },$ and we are also told that $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3.$

To start, let's write down the area formula for the circle and then differentiate it using implicit differentiation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3$ and $r=\frac{5}{2\pi },$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =3\cdot 2\pi (\frac{5}{2\pi }) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the area of the pool is increasing at a rate of $15\,{\text{m}}^{2}\text{/min}.$
